A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work, Kuramoto Orientation Diffusion Models, with 23 readable pages including Appendices A-B. Full text comparison and rendered-page checks establish that differences are confined to the funding acknowledgment and arXiv version/date stamp.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-generation experiments in Section 3, plus coupling ablations, Earth/climate density estimation, and Navier-Stokes generation and forecasting results in Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains the original experimental results in Section 3 and Appendix B, including image-generation scores, ablations, geophysical likelihoods, and fluid forecasting errors.

M1.justification: The global/local Kuramoto dynamics, score-learning objective, wrapped transitions, periodic networks, and Algorithms 1-2 are identical. The amplitude-phase coupling and conditional forecasting procedures in Appendix B.4 are also unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR10, SOCOFing fingerprints, Brodatz textures, ground terrain, four Earth/climate event datasets, and Navier-Stokes fields. Image generation, geophysical density estimation, fluid generation, and forecasting coverage are identical.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in every table, including SGM image baselines, the reference-only ablation, the six comparison methods in Table 8, and the Cartesian and amplitude-phase comparisons in Tables 9-10.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendix B retain identical preprocessing, resolutions, diffusion-step counts, schedules, training settings, metrics, and testing procedures. No existing protocol is revised or new protocol introduced.

E4.justification: The coupling-removal ablation and alternative CMMD evaluation in Appendix B.2 are identical. SNR and generation-trajectory analyses, fluid spectral comparisons, forecasting examples, and supplementary sample grids are also retained unchanged.

E5.justification: Table 8 retains the same five-run averaging statement and uncertainty reporting. No repeated-run information, uncertainty estimation procedure, or statistical reporting practice changes elsewhere.

E6.justification: All numerical entries and qualitative results match, including the 1000-step local-model SOCOFing FID of 18.75 in Table 1 and forecasting MSE of 0.0188 versus SGM's 0.0260 in Table 10. Plots and generated samples are visually identical.

T1.justification: Equations, mathematical assumptions, and derivations are unchanged, including the quasi-equilibrium derivation, local score-matching identity, and Fourier analysis in Appendix A.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about synchronization-based generative modeling, orientation-rich image quality, sampling efficiency, and performance on broader domains.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and qualifications are identical, including the natural-image tradeoff in Section 3.2 and Appendix A.4, training-cost limitations in Section 5, and likelihood-comparison caveat in Appendix B.3.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing instructions, and code/data links are unchanged. The funding acknowledgment revision adds no technical or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: Section 4, research-positioning passages, and all 69 references are identical. The added OpenAI acknowledgment is funding information, not a citation or change in research positioning.

P1.justification: The acknowledgment changes from Cisco supporting Yue Song to the research being supported in part by gifts from Cisco and OpenAI. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; all other wording and document structure remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All 15 figures and 10 tables retain identical content, captions, formatting, and placement. Rendered-page comparison shows no layout revision beyond text reflow within the existing acknowledgment paragraph and the updated margin stamp.

improvement.justification: v3 broadens the funding acknowledgment to include OpenAI and describe support for the research. The scientific content, evidence, reproducibility information, limitations, and visual presentation remain unchanged throughout the main text and appendices, establishing no meaningful overall quality difference.
